topics.title: 2. Algebra and Functions
subtopics: 2.1 Laws of indices for all rational exponents

2.10 Partial fractions (linear and squared linear denominators)

topics.title: 3. Coordinate Geometry in the (x, y) Plane
subtopics: 3.1 Straight lines: y - y1 = m(x - x1), ax + by + c = 0, parallel and perpendicular conditions

topics.title: 4. Sequences and Series
subtopics: 4.1 Binomial expansion of (a + bx)^n for positive integer n and general rational n (|bx/a| < 1)

4.5 Geometric sequences and series: nth term, sum formula, sum to infinity (|r| < 1)

topics.title: 5. Trigonometry
subtopics: 5.1 Sine, cosine, tangent definitions, sine rule, cosine rule, area = 1/2 ab sin C

5.8 Solving trigonometric equations in given intervals
5.9 Trigonometric proofs and identities
5.10 Trigonometric modelling in context

topics.title: 6. Exponentials and Logarithms
subtopics: 6.1 Function a^x and its graph (a > 0)

6.3 Logarithm definition log_a(x), natural logarithm ln(x) as inverse of e^x

6.5 Solving exponential equations a^x = b
6.6 Linearising non-linear laws: y = ax^n and y = kb^x using log graphs
6.7 Exponential growth and decay modelling, limitations and refinements

7.6 Setting up differential equations in pure maths and context

subtopics: 8.1 Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, indefinite integrals

8.8 Differential equation interpretation and modelling in kinematics/context

topics.title: 9. Numerical Methods
subtopics: 9.1 Root location by sign change, conditions for failure

topics.title: 10. Vectors
subtopics: 10.1 2D and 3D vectors: column notation and i, j, k unit vectors

10.3 Vector addition, scalar multiplication, geometric interpretation
10.4 Position vectors, distance between two points in 3D: d^2 = dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2

topics.title: 1. Statistical Sampling

topics.title: 3. Probability
subtopics: 3.1 Mutually exclusive and independent events, Venn and tree diagrams

3.3 Probability modelling and critique of assumptions

topics.title: 4. Statistical Distributions
subtopics: 4.1 Discrete probability distributions, discrete uniform, binomial distribution B(n, p)
4.2 Normal distribution N(mu, sigma^2), calculator usage, inflection points, continuity correction

topics.title: 5. Statistical Hypothesis Testing
subtopics: 5.1 Hypothesis testing vocabulary: H0, H1, significance level, 1-tail/2-tail, critical values/regions, p-values
5.1 Hypothesis test for correlation coefficient using tables/p-values

topics.title: 9. Moments

subtopics: 3.1 Matrix addition, subtraction, multiplication, scalar multiplication

subtopics: 6.1 3D line equations: vector form r = a + lambda*b and Cartesian form

subtopics: 7.1 Polar coordinates (r, theta) and conversion to/from Cartesian (x, y)

subtopics: 8.1 Definitions of sinh x, cosh x, tanh x, graphs, domains and ranges

8.4 Logarithmic forms of inverse hyperbolic functions

subtopics: 9.1 First order linear differential equations using integrating factors: dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x)

9.6 Damped and forced harmonic oscillations, resonance and damping regimes
9.7 Coupled first-order linear simultaneous differential equations (predator-prey / tank models)

topics.title: 3.1 Measurements and their Errors
subtopics: 3.1.1 SI base units, derived units, prefixes (T to f), unit conversions
3.1.2 Random and systematic errors, precision, repeatability, resolution, accuracy

3.1.2 Uncertainties in straight line gradients and intercepts
3.1.3 Orders of magnitude estimations

topics.title: 3.2 Particles and Radiation
subtopics: 3.2.1.1 Constituents of atom, specific charge, nuclide notation, isotopes
3.2.1.2 Strong nuclear force (range, attraction, repulsion), alpha/beta decay, neutrino hypothesis
3.2.1.3 Antimatter, rest energy in MeV, pair production and annihilation
3.2.1.4 Four fundamental interactions, exchange particles (virtual photons, W+, W-)
3.2.1.5 Classification of particles: hadrons (baryons & mesons), leptons, strange particles, quantum numbers
3.2.1.6 Quarks (u, d, s) and antiquarks, baryon/meson composition, neutron decay
3.2.1.7 Conservation laws: charge, baryon number, lepton number, strangeness, momentum, energy
3.2.2.1 Photoelectric effect: threshold frequency, work function, stopping potential, hf = phi + Ek(max)
3.2.2.2 Electron collisions with atoms: excitation, ionisation, eV conversion, fluorescent tube
3.2.2.3 Energy levels and line spectra: hf = E1 - E2
3.2.2.4 Wave-particle duality: electron diffraction, de Broglie wavelength lambda = h/mv

topics.title: 3.3 Waves
subtopics: 3.3.1.1 Progressive waves: amplitude, frequency, wavelength, speed c = f*lambda, phase difference
3.3.1.2 Longitudinal and transverse waves, polarisation and applications
3.3.1.3 Principle of superposition, stationary waves on strings, harmonics f = 1/(2L) * sqrt(T/mu)
3.3.2.1 Interference, coherence, path difference, Young's double slit w = lambda*D/s
3.3.2.2 Single slit diffraction pattern, diffraction grating d sin theta = n lambda
3.3.2.3 Refraction at plane surface: Snell's law, total internal reflection, step-index optical fibres, modal/material dispersion

topics.title: 3.4 Mechanics and Materials
subtopics: 3.4.1.1 Scalars and vectors, addition, resolution, coplanar equilibrium
3.4.1.2 Moments, couples, principle of moments, centre of mass
3.4.1.3 Linear motion: graphs (s-t, v-t, a-t), uniform acceleration SUVAT equations
3.4.1.4 Projectile motion in 2D, fluid friction, terminal speed
3.4.1.5 Newton's laws of motion, F = ma
3.4.1.6 Momentum, impulse F*dt = delta(mv), conservation of linear momentum, elastic/inelastic collisions
3.4.1.7 Work, energy, power P = Fv, efficiency
3.4.1.8 Conservation of mechanical energy: Ep = mgh, Ek = 1/2 mv^2
3.4.2.1 Bulk solids: density rho = m/V, Hooke's law F = k*delta_L, stress, strain, elastic strain energy = 1/2 F*delta_L
3.4.2.2 Young modulus E = (FL)/(A*delta_L), stress-strain graphs

topics.title: 3.5 Electricity
subtopics: 3.5.1.1 Current I = delta_Q/delta_t, pd V = W/Q, resistance R = V/I
3.5.1.2 I-V characteristics: ohmic conductor, semiconductor diode, filament lamp; Ohm's law
3.5.1.3 Resistivity rho = RA/L, temperature effect on metals and NTC thermistors, superconductivity
3.5.1.4 Series and parallel circuits: Kirchhoff's laws, power P = IV = I^2 R = V^2/R
3.5.1.5 Potential dividers, sensor circuits (LDR, thermistor)
3.5.1.6 EMF and internal resistance: epsilon = I(R + r), terminal pd

topics.title: 3.6 Further Mechanics and Thermal Physics
subtopics: 3.6.1.1 Circular motion: angular speed omega = v/r = 2*pi*f, centripetal acceleration a = v^2/r, centripetal force F = mv^2/r
3.6.1.2 Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM): a = -omega^2 x, x = A cos(omega*t), v = +/- omega*sqrt(A^2 - x^2)
3.6.1.3 SHM systems: mass-spring T = 2*pi*sqrt(m/k), simple pendulum T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g), energy exchange
3.6.1.4 Free and forced vibrations, resonance, damping
3.6.2.1 Thermal energy transfer: internal energy, first law of thermodynamics, Q = mc*delta_theta, latent heat Q = ml
3.6.2.2 Ideal gases: gas laws, absolute zero, pV = nRT, pV = NkT, work done = p*delta_V
3.6.2.3 Molecular kinetic theory: Brownian motion, derivation of pV = 1/3 N m (c_rms)^2, kinetic energy = 3/2 kT

topics.title: 3.7 Fields and their Consequences
subtopics: 3.7.1 Gravitational vs electrostatic force fields: similarities and differences
3.7.2.1 Newton's law of gravitation: F = G m1 m2 / r^2
3.7.2.2 Gravitational field strength g = GM/r^2, radial and uniform fields
3.7.2.3 Gravitational potential V = -GM/r, potential difference, equipotential surfaces, g = -dV/dr
3.7.2.4 Planetary and satellite orbits: Kepler's third law T^2 proportional to r^3, escape velocity, geostationary orbits
3.7.3.1 Coulomb's law: F = (1/(4*pi*epsilon_0)) * (Q1*Q2 / r^2)
3.7.3.2 Electric field strength E = F/Q, uniform field E = V/d, radial field E = Q/(4*pi*epsilon_0*r^2)
3.7.3.3 Electric potential V = Q/(4*pi*epsilon_0*r), potential gradient E = -dV/dr
3.7.4.1 Capacitance C = Q/V
3.7.4.2 Parallel plate capacitor C = A*epsilon_0*epsilon_r / d, dielectric action
3.7.4.3 Energy stored in a capacitor: E = 1/2 QV = 1/2 CV^2 = 1/2 Q^2/C
3.7.4.4 Capacitor charge and discharge curves, time constant RC, half-life T_{1/2} = 0.69 RC, exponential decay Q = Q0 e^{-t/RC}
3.7.5.1 Magnetic flux density B, force on wire F = BIl, Fleming's left hand rule
3.7.5.2 Force on moving charge F = BQv, circular trajectory, cyclotron
3.7.5.3 Magnetic flux phi = BA, flux linkage N*phi = BAN cos theta
3.7.5.4 Electromagnetic induction: Faraday's and Lenz's laws, induced emf epsilon = N delta_phi/delta_t, rotating coil epsilon = BAN*omega*sin(omega*t)
3.7.5.5 Alternating currents: rms values Irms = I0/sqrt(2), Vrms = V0/sqrt(2), oscilloscope usage
3.7.5.6 Transformers: Ns/Np = Vs/Vp, efficiency, eddy currents, high-voltage grid transmission

topics.title: 3.8 Nuclear Physics
subtopics: 3.8.1.1 Rutherford alpha scattering experiment, nuclear model
3.8.1.2 Alpha, beta, gamma radiation: properties, absorption, inverse-square law for gamma, background radiation
3.8.1.3 Radioactive decay law: dN/dt = -lambda*N, N = N0 e^{-lambda*t}, activity A = lambda*N, half-life T_{1/2} = ln(2)/lambda
3.8.1.4 Nuclear instability: N-Z curve, alpha/beta+/beta- decay, electron capture, gamma emission, metastable Tc-99m
3.8.1.5 Nuclear radius: closest approach method, electron diffraction method, R = R0 A^{1/3}, constant nuclear density
3.8.1.6 Mass and energy equivalence: E = mc^2, mass defect, binding energy, 1 u = 931.5 MeV, binding energy per nucleon curve
3.8.1.7 Induced nuclear fission: thermal neutrons, chain reaction, critical mass, moderator, control rods, coolant
3.8.1.8 Nuclear reactor safety: shielding, remote handling, radioactive waste disposal

topics.title: Required Practical Activities
subtopics: RP1: Frequency of stationary waves on a string with length, tension and mass per unit length
RP2: Investigation of interference effects: Young's slit and diffraction grating
RP3: Determination of g by a free-fall method
RP4: Determination of the Young modulus by a simple method

RP6: Investigation of emf and internal resistance of electric cells
RP7: Simple harmonic motion using mass-spring system and simple pendulum
RP8: Boyle's law and Charles's law for a gas
RP9: Charge and discharge of capacitors and determination of RC time constant

RP11: Magnetic flux linkage variation with search coil angle using oscilloscope
RP12: Inverse-square law for gamma radiation

subjects.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science

topics.title: 1. Information Representation
subtopics: 1.1 Data Representation: number bases, two's complement, binary arithmetic, overflow, BCD, hexadecimal, ASCII, Unicode
1.2 Multimedia: bitmap images (resolution, bit depth, calculations), vector graphics (drawing list, properties), sound sampling
1.3 Compression: lossy vs lossless, run-length encoding (RLE), text/image/sound compression

topics.title: 2. Communication
subtopics: 2.1 Networks: LAN, WAN, client-server vs peer-to-peer, thin vs thick client
2.1 Topologies: bus, star, mesh, hybrid
2.1 Cloud computing: public vs private, benefits and risks
2.1 Wired vs wireless transmission media, network hardware (switch, router, NIC, WAP)
2.1 Ethernet CSMA/CD, bit streaming, IP addressing (IPv4/IPv6, subnetting, public/private, static/dynamic), URL & DNS

topics.title: 3. Hardware
subtopics: 3.1 Hardware components: input/output devices, secondary storage (magnetic, optical, solid state), embedded systems
3.1 RAM vs ROM, SRAM vs DRAM, PROM/EPROM/EEPROM, sensors & actuators in monitoring and control
3.2 Logic Gates & Circuits: NOT, AND, OR, NAND, NOR, XOR truth tables, logic expressions and circuit diagrams

topics.title: 4. Processor Fundamentals
subtopics: 4.1 CPU Architecture: Von Neumann model, system clock, buses (data, address, control), registers (PC, MAR, MDR, ACC, IX, CIR, Status)
4.1 Fetch-Execute cycle, register transfer notation, interrupts and ISR handling
4.2 Assembly Language: two-pass assembler, addressing modes (immediate, direct, indirect, indexed, relative), instruction tracing
4.3 Bit manipulation: logical/arithmetic/cyclic shifts, bitwise operations (AND, OR, XOR), masking

topics.title: 5. System Software
subtopics: 5.1 Operating Systems: memory, file, security, hardware, process management; utility software; dynamic link libraries (DLL)
5.2 Language Translators: assemblers, compilers, interpreters; IDE features (debugger, syntax check, prettyprint)

topics.title: 6. Security, Privacy and Data Integrity
subtopics: 6.1 Data security: threats (malware, phishing, pharming), security measures (firewalls, passwords, biometrics, encryption)
6.2 Data integrity: validation methods (range, format, length, presence, check digit), verification (double entry, parity, checksum)

topics.title: 7. Ethics and Ownership
subtopics: 7.1 Professional ethics (BCS, IEEE), copyright legislation, software licenses (open source, shareware, commercial), AI impacts

topics.title: 8. Databases
subtopics: 8.1 Relational database concepts: entities, keys (primary, foreign, candidate), ER diagrams, normalisation (1NF, 2NF, 3NF)
8.2 DBMS functions: data dictionary, query processor, data modelling, security
8.3 SQL DDL: CREATE/ALTER TABLE, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY
8.3 SQL DML: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, INNER JOIN, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

topics.title: 9. Algorithm Design and Problem-solving
subtopics: 9.1 Computational thinking: abstraction, decomposition
9.2 Algorithms: pseudocode, flowcharts, structured English, stepwise refinement, identifier tables

topics.title: 10. Data Types and Structures
subtopics: 10.1 Data types and record structures
10.2 Arrays: 1D and 2D arrays, linear search, bubble sort
10.3 File handling: reading and writing text files
10.4 Abstract Data Types: stack, queue, linked list implementations using arrays

topics.title: 11. Programming
subtopics: 11.1 Programming basics: variable/constant declaration, operators, built-in string functions
11.2 Control constructs: IF-THEN-ELSE, CASE, count-controlled (FOR), pre-condition (WHILE), post-condition (REPEAT)
11.3 Structured programming: procedures, functions, parameters by value vs by reference

topics.title: 12. Software Development
subtopics: 12.1 Program development lifecycle models: waterfall, iterative, RAD
12.2 Program design: structure charts, state-transition diagrams
12.3 Testing & maintenance: syntax/logic/runtime errors, dry run, white/black box, test plans, corrective/adaptive/perfective maintenance

topics.title: 13. Data Representation (Advanced)
subtopics: 13.1 User-defined types: enumerated, pointer, record, set, classes
13.2 File organisation: serial, sequential, random access; hashing algorithms
13.3 Floating-point numbers: two's complement mantissa & exponent, normalisation, overflow/underflow, rounding errors

topics.title: 14. Communication and Internet Technologies
subtopics: 14.1 Protocols: TCP/IP four-layer model, application protocols (HTTP, FTP, SMTP, POP3, IMAP, BitTorrent)
14.2 Packet switching vs circuit switching, router operations

topics.title: 15. Hardware and Virtual Machines
subtopics: 15.1 Processors: RISC vs CISC, pipelining, Flynn's taxonomy (SISD, SIMD, MISD, MIMD), virtual machines
15.2 Boolean algebra: half/full adders, SR & JK flip-flops, De Morgan's laws, Karnaugh maps (K-maps)

topics.title: 16. System Software (Advanced)
subtopics: 16.1 Operating System kernel: process management (ready/running/blocked), scheduling algorithms, virtual memory, paging, segmentation, thrashing
16.2 Translation software: lexical analysis, syntax analysis, code generation, optimisation, BNF and syntax diagrams, RPN

topics.title: 17. Security (Advanced)
subtopics: 17.1 Asymmetric/symmetric cryptography, public/private keys, quantum cryptography, SSL/TLS handshake, digital certificates

topics.title: 18. Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: 18.1 AI: graph searches (A* and Dijkstra), artificial neural networks, deep/reinforcement/supervised learning, back-propagation

sections.name: A Level Further Problem-solving & Programming (Paper 4 Practical)

topics.title: 19. Computational Thinking and Problem-solving
subtopics: 19.1 Algorithms: linear & binary search, insertion & bubble sort, Big-O time and space complexity
19.1 ADT algorithms: linked list, binary tree, stack, queue traversal, insertion, and deletion
19.2 Recursion: base cases, stack frames, unwinding, recursive algorithm tracing and implementation

topics.title: 20. Further Programming
subtopics: 20.1 Programming paradigms: low-level, imperative, OOP (classes, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism), declarative
20.2 File processing (serial, sequential, random) and structured exception handling in Python
